title: LVMH sales at key unit fall as China woes hurt Louis Vuitton
article:
(Oct 12): LVMH’s biggest division posted a slump in sales last quarter as its key Louis Vuitton brand suffered from a boycott in China.

Organic revenue at the fashion and leather goods unit slid 5% in the third quarter, LVMH Moët Hennessy Louis Vuitton SE said in a statement on Monday. Analysts were expecting a drop of 1.57%.

The division was “affected in the third quarter by the slowdown in demand in China,” LVMH said.

Louis Vuitton sales suffered in July and August in China after the brand won a trademark dispute against Molly Tea, a local tea maker, Bloomberg reported last month. The victory drew a backlash from Chinese consumers there who deemed it unfair of the world’s largest luxury group to take the much smaller company to court.

LVMH shares have fallen by more than 40% this year, putting them on track for the worst annual performance since the global financial crisis in 2008. While much of the industry is feeling the effects of the downturn in demand, LVMH’s stock is the worst performer this year among major luxury groups, followed by rival Hermes International SCA.

Hopes for a rebound in the wider luxury industry this year have been undermined by sluggish Chinese demand, the prolonged conflict in the Middle East and weaker consumer confidence.

Aedge acquires corner terraced property on Westerhout Road  for $7.5 mil
article:
Aedge Group, through its wholly-owned subsidiary IPF Investments, has acquired a freehold corner terraced property located at 2 Westerhout Road in the Geylang-Eunos precinct. It was purchased for $7.5 million, the Singapore-listed group said in an Oct 12 bourse filing.

The acquisition is part of its growth strategy to diversify revenue and enhance shareholder value through its investment properties division, the group added. Aedge also provides engineering, transportation, security and manpower services.

The Westerhout Road property occupies 297.4 sq m (3,201 sq ft) of land in District 14 that is zoned for “Commercial / Institution” use, according to URA Space, the land authority’s web-based map service.

“Freehold commercial properties of this kind are rare, and we believe the purchase price represents an attractive entry point relative to recent comparable freehold transactions in District 14,” said Poh Soon Keng, Aedge’s executive chairman and CEO.

Poh added that the site offers longer-term redevelopment and asset-enhancement potential, given its proximity to the Paya Lebar commercial hub and the ongoing transformation of the Geylang corridor.

The deal represents Aedge’s fourth property acquisition, and its first commercial asset.

In October 2023, Aedge completed the acquisition of 9 Tuas South Street 11 for $9 million. Now known as Amethyst House, the property comprises a detached factory, workshops and a 299-bed secondary workers’ dormitory (SWD), according to the company’s website.

In 2024, Aedge purchased 4 Tuas South Street (now Beryl House) for $8.5 million. The site comprises a four-storey detached warehouse with ramp-up access and a 408-bed SWD.

Earlier this year, the group completed the acquisition of 219 Kallang Bahru (Carnelian House), an eight-storey industrial building, for $13.99 million.

title: Real estate investment sales set to hit new record in 2026: Knight Frank Singapore
article:
Singapore real estate investment sales are poised to hit an all-time annual high in 2026, according to research by Knight Frank Singapore.

Data in an October report shows investment sales totalled $10.7 billion in 3Q2026, moderating from the $16.2 billion and $15.5 billion logged in the first and second quarters.

Still, it brings the sales volume tally to $42.4 billion for the first nine months of the year, already surpassing the record-setting $40.7 billion achieved for the whole of 2025.

Consequently, the stage is set for 2026 to achieve “a new all-time record”, said Melvin Chay, Knight Frank Singapore’s interim head for capital markets. Knight Frank Singapore estimates total investment sales could reach around the $50 billion mark this year.

This comes as Chay expects transaction momentum to “remain healthy” in 4Q2026, supported by “several large ticket deals presently in due diligence”.

“As there are expectations of rate hikes leading to increased borrowing costs, parties involved in ongoing negotiations might be motivated to complete their transactions by year-end,” he added.

Residential deals led investment activity in 3Q2026 at $4.3 billion, overtaking commercial transactions, which had topped volumes for the previous three consecutive quarters.

The bulk of residential investment sales last quarter came from Government Land Sales, along with the sale of a site at 8 Thomson Lane to a Sustained Land-led consortium for around $1 billion (including land betterment charges).

Commercial investment sales totalled $2 billion in 3Q2026, largely underpinned by two deals involving Orchard Road assets.

The first was Hongkong Land Holdings’ $1.1 billion acquisition of Wheelock Place , a commercial building with office and retail space, through its Singapore Central Private Real Estate Fund in July. The second deal was the $310 million purchase of Scotts Square mall by Royal Holdings and RB Capital.

The industrial sector saw higher investment activity, with transaction value clocking in at $2 billion in 3Q2026 – more than double the previous quarter.

Deals were anchored by public sector land sales, with JTC awarding three Business 2 industrial sites at Jalan Buroh, Kaki Bukit and 5 Tuas Avenue for $214.4 million, $52.8 million and $43.4 million respectively during the quarter.

In addition, two purpose-built worker dormitory sites at Kranji Close and Lok Yang Way were awarded for $343 million and $221.7 million, respectively.

The living and hospitality sector recorded a sole transaction in 3Q2026: the sale of Coliwoo Midtown , a 212-key co-living property on Middle Road, to CapitaLand Ascott Trust for $134 million ($632,075 per key).

Nonetheless, hotel transactions have totalled $1.5 billion across seven deals for the first nine months of the year, exceeding the $957.2 million value (across nine deals) logged for the whole of 2025, Knight Frank highlights.

title: Middle Road commercial building for sale at $80 mil
article:
A 999-year leasehold commercial building at 45 Middle Road is up for sale through an expression of interest (EOI) exercise with a guide price of $80 million.

The six-storey property, also known as Foo Ann Building , has a land area of 5,554 sq ft and a gross floor area (GFA) of about 25,493 sq ft.

Based on the GFA, the guide price works out to $3,138 psf. As a commercial property, the asset is not subject to additional buyer’s stamp duty or foreign ownership restrictions.

Checks online indicate that levels 1 to 5 of the building currently serve as the campus for Academies Australasia College, an education provider offering programmes ranging from preparatory to degree and postgraduate courses.

Located in the Beach Road-Bugis precinct, the building is close to several landmarks and lifestyle amenities, including the National Library, Raffles Hotel and Bugis Junction . It is also within walking distance of the Bugis, Bras Basah and City Hall MRT stations.

The building’s strategic location, coupled with its 999-year tenure, offers investors a compelling proposition for redevelopment or asset repositioning, commented Yeo Khee Liang, associate senior marketing director at Huttons Asia, in an October release.

Lee Sze Teck, Huttons’ senior director of data analytics, added that buyers could consider converting the building into office, hospitality or co-living spaces.

The EOI will close at 3pm on Dec 7.

title: This ryokan‑style home looks straight out of Japan — but it’s an EC in Singapore
article:
Japanese influences run throughout Miya and Jason's three-bedroom-plus-study unit at the North Gaia executive condo (EC) in Yishun.

Shoji- inspired panels line parts of the home, all three bedrooms have sliding doors, and a stone lantern greets visitors at the entrance.

On the balcony, the family eats around a low dining table in a setting that reminds the homeowners of the old-school Japanese restaurants from their travels.

Elsewhere, there is a cosy corner underneath a loft bed for their 10-year-old son to read and play.

The 1,076 sq ft home houses Miya, 41, an accountant, her husband Jason, 39, an army regular, and their son, Mikael. The family moved into the apartment in January this year, following an $80,000 renovation that included electrical works.

In love with all things Japan

For the couple, the Japanese references are personal. They travel to Japan regularly, so much so that Miya says her colleagues call the country her "second home".

When it came to their own home, they wanted to recreate some of that feeling without losing sight of the practical needs of a family of three.

"We are very chill," Miya says. "I need a home that feels cosy and comfortable."

But cosy does not mean dark and sleepy — Miya says she still needs light that is bright enough to be able to work at home and for her son to do his homework in the different spaces.

Storage was another priority, as the family owns plenty of clothes, shoes, jewellery and other belongings, and Miya wanted as much of it as possible tucked away.

"We need a lot of storage to hide [our belongings] so that we don't see the mess," she says.

A decade to figure out what they want

Before North Gaia, the family lived in a four-room HDB flat for about a decade. It was Miya and Jason's first home together, and Jason was working overseas when it was being put together.

Miya describes the process as “largely DIY”. Family members helped with the painting, and she had little idea then of what she wanted.

"I didn't know what to do," she recalls. "I was completely easygoing with the renovation, with help and advice from my family in the construction business. Aesthetics were not even a consideration back then."

Living there for 10 years gave the couple a clearer idea of what they wanted from their next home.

As a result, when they bought their second home, Miya had a list of priorities for the renovation: good lighting, extensive storage, no wasted corners and a consistent Japanese-inspired interior.

She was also approaching this EC unit’s renovation with a much longer horizon.

"I don't wish to move anymore in my entire life. Due to the amount of things we have, I hate shifting houses. I plan to stay here forever, [so] I decided to get a proper interior designer," she says.

She adds with a laugh that her husband had even become increasingly exasperated by the search for an interior designer, as Miya’s expectations were high.

The couple met around 10 interior designers before settling on one: Yang’s Inspiration Design.

Memory of Kusatsu

Miya knew she wanted a Japanese-inspired home, but one of the clearest references came from a family trip to Kusatsu Onsen in Japan.

They struggled to find their way to the remote town, getting lost in the dark and snow. By the time they finally arrived, they were exhausted.

Stepping into the ryokan , a traditional Japanese inn, and soaking in the onsen after the difficult journey left an impression on Miya. “It was the best thing after a hectic day,” she recalls.

It was that sense of relief and calm that the couple wanted to recreate at home: a place where they could leave the bustle of the day behind once they stepped through the door.

When Miya was choosing an interior designer, she met with around 10 firms and compared their proposals for the home. While many had similar ideas for the main living area, Dexter Lim from Yang’s Inspiration Design stood out for his treatment of the corridor, which reminded her of that experience in Kusatsu.

“The corridor vibes he gave me were the exact same as what I had felt at the onsen ,” she says.

Finding room for everything

The family did not make major changes to the unit's original layout. Much of the work instead involved making better use of the space available.

"I need a lot of custom carpentry," says Miya. "We want to utilise all corners and don't want any dead space."

At the foyer, she had two requirements: a place for their Japanese stone lantern, and a privacy screen of sorts that would prevent passersby from looking directly into the unit when the front door was open.

The three bedrooms, meanwhile, were fitted with sliding doors. The Shoji -inspired panels carry the Japanese reference further into the interior.

Miya and Jason have also accumulated a sizeable collection of figurines, given their interest in anime. Miya felt the colourful collection would compete with the rest of the interior, so most of it was given a home of its own in the games room.

"My figurines don't exactly match the theme of my house, so they must be hidden in the room, for my own enjoyment," she says.

Ironically, the room initially meant just to contain the things Miya wanted to keep out of sight has become the space she now uses most.

She works, watches television and plays games there. Since moving in January 2026, she estimates she has slept in the master bedroom fewer than four nights.

"I spend more time there than my master bedroom," she admits.

A room that can grow with their son

Their son's bedroom was likewise planned for the long run.

The 10-year-old initially gravitated towards brighter colours, including blue, but his parents ultimately made the design decisions.

"Mikael’s room needs to be designed in a way so he won’t be embarrassed to bring his friends home, be it when he’s 10 or 20," she says.

A loft bed frees up the floor space below to create a cosy nook for him to read and play with his toys.

Dinners at the balcony

Instead of trying to squeeze a dining area into the main living space, Miya and Jason made use of the balcony, which might otherwise have served as a laundry area.

With its low, sit-down arrangement, the space unexpectedly took on another Japanese reference. To Miya, it resembles the traditional restaurants in Japan. "Once you sit down, you won't wish to stand back up," she says.

There is no room in the house she considers her favourite. She works and unwinds in the games room, and the family gathers for meals on the balcony.  “I love every single part of the house!” she exclaims, reiterating her hope that this will be their forever home.

title: Frasers Hospitality opens Fraser Place Roppongi, Tokyo
article:
Frasers Hospitality, a business unit of Frasers Property, has announced the opening of Fraser Place Roppongi, Tokyo, expanding its presence in Japan.

Located in the Minato district, the serviced residence offers 172 rooms ranging from studios to one- and two-bedroom apartments. Each residence has a kitchenette, an in-room washing machine and complimentary WiFi.

Guests also have access to a residents’ lounge and co-working hub, an indoor gym, meeting spaces and a daily breakfast service.

The new property strengthens Frasers Hospitality’s presence in Japan, building on Fraser Residence Nankai Osaka, noted outgoing CEO Eu Chin Fen in an Oct 12 release. Last week, Frasers Hospitality announced she would be stepping down from her role as CEO of Frasers Hospitality , effective Jan 1, 2027.

Eu added that the new property reflects Frasers Hospitality's approach of entering markets with strong international appeal and tailoring its serviced living offerings to each location.

The 114-room Fraser Residence Nakai Osaka opened in 2010. It marked Frasers' first serviced apartment in Japan.

Frasers Hospitality currently has a portfolio of over 100 properties across 19 countries.

In Japan, its properties also include Ana Crowne Plaza Kobe, a 593-room hotel in Kobe City; Estem Court Namba VII Beyond Osaka, a 124-key premium rental apartment; and the 244-key Yotel Tokyo Ginza.

A REIT’s yield can rise because distributions are growing, but it can also increase simply because the unit price has fallen.
That is why a high yield deserves a closer look.
A weaker unit price may reflect concerns about softer rental income, rising interest costs or pressure on future distributions.
Here are three
Singapore-listed REITs
yielding more than 6%, each with a different set of opportunities and risks.
Frasers Logistics & Commercial Trust (SGX: BUOU)
Frasers Logistics & Commercial Trust, or FLCT, owns logistics, industrial and commercial properties across Australia, Europe and Singapore.
The REIT’s latest half-year results were steady.
For the first half of its financial year 2026 ended 31 March 2026 (1HFY2026), revenue rose by 2.8% year on year (YoY) to S$238.9 million.
Adjusted net property income (NPI) also increased by 3.6% YoY to S$167 million over the same period.
The improvement was driven partly by positive rental reversions and annual rent increases in its Australian and European logistics portfolios.
A full half-year of income from a Singapore logistics property bought in November 2024 and stronger foreign currencies also helped.
For 1HFY2026, headline distribution per unit (DPU) declined 1.7% YoY to S$0.0295.
The weaker headline DPU partly reflected lower distributions from divestment gains.
However, excluding these divestment-related distributions, DPU jumped 11.9% YoY to S$0.0282.
As at 30 June 2026, FLCT’s balance sheet remained relatively comfortable, with aggregate leverage at 35.4% and interest coverage ratio (ICR) at 4.6 times.
In July 2026, unitholders approved the REIT’s S$441.5 million acquisition of four logistics properties in Germany and the Netherlands.
The deal will be fully funded by borrowings, and FLCT estimates its aggregate leverage will rise to around 38.7% once the purchase is completed.
Investors should watch how this affects financing costs.
Across its latest two half-year periods, the trust distributed a total of S$0.059 per unit.
Based on its closing price of S$0.87 on 9 October 2026, this translates to a trailing distribution yield of approximately 6.8%.

Sasseur REIT (SGX: CRPU)
Sasseur REIT invests in retail properties, offering investors exposure to outlet malls in China.
Unlike conventional retail REITs that rely mainly on fixed rental payments, Sasseur operates under an entrusted management agreement (EMA).
The arrangement combines a fixed rental component with a variable component linked to outlet sales.
This model thus allows the REIT to benefit when consumer spending at its malls increases.
For 1H2026 ended 30 June 2026, EMA rental income rose by 4.3% YoY to RMB350.7 million.
The rise was supported by a 7.4% YoY jump in portfolio sales to RMB2.34 billion.
According to the 1H2026 presentation, the conversion of former cinema space at the Hefei Outlet into a new retail precinct was nearing completion as of June 2026.
Demand for the new space was encouraging: 11 of the 13 retail units already pre-committed, with openings scheduled from August 2026.
The project could help Sasseur lift sales from existing assets without relying on property acquisitions.
The REIT’s balance sheet also remained relatively strong.
Aggregate leverage stood at 25.6% while ICR reached a robust 5.6 times.
For 1H2026, Sasseur’s DPU increased 10.2% YoY to S$0.03366.
Despite its recent growth, Sasseur faces an important contractual uncertainty.
Ahead of its April 2026 annual general meeting, management said it was still considering its options for the EMA, which expires in 2028.
Any changes to the EMA could affect the stability of future distributions.
Sasseur’s latest two half-year distributions amounted to S$0.06449 per unit.
At a closing price of S$0.63 on 9 October 2026, this translates to a trailing distribution yield of approximately 10.2%.
Related articles:
Top 4 S-REITs Raising DPU by 10% or More
5 High-Yield Singapore Stocks: Are Their Dividends Really Safe?
ESR-REIT (SGX: 9A4U)
ESR-REIT owns a mix of industrial, logistics and business park properties across Singapore, Australia and Japan.
For 1H2026, gross revenue came in at S$222.3 million, down 0.3% from a year earlier.
The REIT also reported a 2.2% YoY decline in NPI to S$162.7 million.
However, part of that decline reflects ESR-REIT’s ongoing portfolio-reshaping efforts.
Across FY2025 and 1H2026, the REIT sold 10 non-core Singapore properties, which reduced rental income.
The manager plans to recycle the proceeds into six freehold logistics properties in Australia.
Looking only at the remaining portfolio, performance was more resilient, with same-store revenue up 2.3% YoY and NPI rising 0.7% YoY.
For 1H2026, portfolio occupancy stood at 91.9% and rental reversions reached 9.8%.
Despite the decline in headline property income, total DPU increased 2.4% YoY to S$0.1151.
Core DPU, which excludes one-off gains, rose 4.5% YoY to S$0.1125 and made up about 98% of the payout.
Regarding its risk exposure, aggregate leverage stood at 41.4% with its ICR at 2.6 times.
This makes refinancing costs and debt management more important considerations.
Separately, in August 2026, ESR-REIT disclosed that an Australian tenant contributing about 5.2% of its effective gross rents had defaulted on rent and entered administration.
After drawing on bank guarantees, the REIT unrecovered arrears would fall from roughly A$12.2 million to about A$1.5 million.
However, a prolonged vacancy at the three leased properties could still weigh on rental income.
Over its latest two half-year periods, ESR-REIT paid out S$0.22185 per unit.
At its S$2.02 closing price on 9 October 2026, that works out to a trailing distribution yield of about 11%.

Putting the yield into context
A high yield naturally stands out, but the number needs some context.
The benchmark 10-year Singapore Government Security yielded 2.45% on 9 October 2026, far below the yields offered by three REITs.

title: Seatrium Launches a S$200 Million Share Buyback: Is the Stock Worth a Look?
article:
Seatrium Limited
(SGX: 5E2) has announced a new
S$200 million share buyback
programme, doubling its latest buyback programme (completed on 1 September 2026), and funded from existing cash.
This latest announcement continues the buybacks Seatrium has already undertaken, making it more important than a one-off announcement.
With shares currently trading around S$2, is this just a capital-return exercise or part of the investment case?
Metric / Area
Summary
Stock Name & Ticker
Seatrium Limited
(SGX: 5E2)
Share Buyback
S$200 million programme funded by cash
Current 2% mandate limits repurchases to ~68 million shares (~S$136 million at S$2/share)
Financial Performance
1H2026 revenue up 5% YoY to to S$5.6 billion
Net profit up 158% to S$373 million (up 54% to S$212 million excluding divestment gains)
Gross margin expanded to 8.6%
Order Book Pipeline
Net order book of of S$13.3 billion across 24 projects through 2033; chasing a pipeline of >S$32 billion
Balance Sheet & Cash Flow
S$3.4 billion liquidity
Net leverage at 0.5x
Gross debt of S$2.4 billion
Underlying 1H2026 free cash flow was -S$11 million excluding asset sales and settlements
Valuation
S$2.00 share price (~S$7.1 billion market cap)
Forward P/E: 13.9x
P/B: 0.9x
What Exactly Has Seatrium Announced?
The buyback’s pace will depend on Seatrium’s share price, market conditions and capital priorities.
This programme runs under a shareholder mandate that allows repurchases of up to 2% of issued shares and requires approval at each annual general meeting.
The first programme launched in April 2024 took about 28 months to complete.
Under that earlier programme, repurchased shares were held as treasury shares.
These treasury shares can be used for employee share plans and directors’ fees, or cancelled against share capital.
This new programme is described as supporting both shareholder returns and employee incentives.
In the first nine months of 2026, Seatrium’s purchases averaged about S$2.12 a share, compared with about S$1.77 for the first repurchase in June 2024.
Why Do Companies Buy Back Their Own Shares?
A buyback enhances shareholder returns alongside
dividends
.
By reducing the shares outstanding, each remaining shareholder owns a bigger slice of the company and earnings per share (EPS) rise if profit holds steady.
It can also signal that management thinks the shares are worth more than the market price, though this is not proof.
Buybacks only create value if the price paid is sensible and the cash isn’t required elsewhere.
Related articles:
Top 3 Temasek-Backed Stocks With Aggressive Share Buybacks
Top 6 Temasek-Backed Stocks With Aggressive Share Buybacks
What Has Been Happening at Seatrium?
Beyond its buyback, what has Seatrium been reporting?
For the six months ended 30 June 2026 (1H2026), revenue rose 5% year on year (YoY) to S$5.6 billion.
Net profit was S$373 million, up 158%, but this figure includes divestment gains.
Excluding divestment gains, net profit rose 54% YoY to S$212 million, helped by gross margin widening from 7.4% to 8.6% on a higher-margin project mix and lower costs.
EBITDA excluding divestments rose 20% YoY to S$479 million.
As of 30 June 2026, Seatrium’s net order book was S$13.3 billion, spanning 24 projects through 2033.
This represents a softening from S$17.8 billion as at 31 December 2025, as work done on existing projects outpaced new orders.
The group is chasing a pipeline of more than S$32 billion and holds a letter of intent from
Golar LNG Limited
(NASDAQ: GLNG) for a third floating LNG conversion, with a contract expected to be signed in 2H2026.
Seatrium’s balance sheet looks healthy, supported by S$3.4 billion in liquidity.
From December 2025, gross debt fell 5% to S$2.4 billion, while net debt held steady at S$680 million.
Net finance costs dropped 20% YoY to S$43 million, while net leverage improved to 0.5x (from 0.8x as at 31 December 2025).
Operationally, it completed its seventh conversion of an LNG carrier into a floating storage regasification unit (FSRU) for Karpowership in September and is pursuing energy-transition work such as offshore wind.
Is the S$200 Million Buyback Material?
S$200 million equals about 2.8% of Seatrium’s S$7.1 billion market value.
At S$2 a share, S$200 million would buy roughly 100 million shares, about 2.9% of the 3.39 billion outstanding.
But the current mandate caps buybacks at 2% of issued shares, roughly 68 million shares or about S$136 million at today’s price.
Spending the rest depends on shareholders renewing the mandate at future AGMs.
If the repurchased shares were cancelled, EPS would rise by a similar percentage, all else being equal.
Shares reissued to employees, however, would not shrink the share count.
Ultimately, a buyback does not guarantee share price appreciation, nor does it replace the need for sustained earnings and cash flow growth.
The Biggest Question: Can Seatrium Generate Enough Cash?
This is the real test.
Excluding a one-off S$73 million legal settlement, operating cash flow for 1H2026 was S$114 million, still thin compared to underlying profit.
Capital expenditure (capex) was S$52 million, mainly on project needs and safety requirements.
Subtracting capex leaves free cash flow (FCF) of roughly negative S$11 million.
Seatrium reported a headline FCF of S$237 million, that figure relied on S$167 million in asset sales.
How Does Seatrium’s Stock Move From Here?
Seatrium must convert new and existing orders into revenue and cash flows while maintaining execution margins.
Watch buyback activity and improving sentiment towards Seatrium’s offshore and marine operations.
The buyback is a reason to look at the stock, not the reason to own it.
What Could Go Wrong?
If projects overrun or are delayed, Seatrium’s margins would take a direct hit.
Large projects also absorb working capital before payments arrive, which could pressure cash flows.
Higher interest rates would raise Seatrium’s financing costs, though the impact would be limited: 64% of its debt was at fixed rates as of 30 June 2026.
Offshore spending is also highly cyclical, which could derail Seatrium’s financial results.
If earnings falter, shares repurchased today could prove to have been expensive.
Is Seatrium’s Stock Cheap After the Buyback Announcement?
As of 9 October 2026, Seatrium’s shares closed at S$2, giving it a market capitalisation of S$7.1 billion.
That values the company at roughly 13.9x forward earnings, with a price-to-book (P/B) ratio at roughly 0.9x.
These
valuations
are within historical ranges.
By comparison,
Yangzijiang Shipbuilding (Holdings) Ltd.
(SGX: BS6) trades at about 2.1x book value.
On these measures, Seatrium’s valuation looks reasonable rather than cheap.

Get Smart: A Buyback Is a Signal, Not the Investment Case
The S$200 million programme is a bigger commitment than the last and could lift EPS.
But the headline figure is larger than the mandate can deliver at today’s price; first-half free cash flow leaned on asset sales.
The turnaround is real in margins and profit, but still has to show up in operating cash flow and new orders.
The buyback is a reason to look at the stock, not the reason to own it.

title: Singapore Bank Shares Have Fallen. Are They Cheap Enough Yet?
article:
Three trading days.
That was all it took for Singapore’s bank shares to give back over two months of gains.
The sell-off began last Wednesday (7 October), and coincided with Citi downgrading
Oversea-Chinese Banking Corporation
(SGX: O39), or OCBC, from neutral to sell.
OCBC shares fell by over 5% that day.
DBS Group Holdings
(SGX: D05) and
United Overseas Bank
(SGX: U11), or UOB, fell 1.4% and 2.9% respectively.
By Friday’s close, OCBC shares sat around 11% below their 52-week high. UOB was down by close to 11% and DBS by 7.2%.
If you own bank shares, you don’t need to panic.
As bad as it gets?
The drop feels sharp because it came so fast.
Widen the lens from three days to three months, and DBS and OCBC shares sit roughly where they traded in late July.
The three banks make up 57% of the
Straits Times Index
(SGX: ^STI), or STI.
That index ended Friday only around 7.3% below its 52-week high.
In other words, we’re not at a 10% decline yet, so we’re not in market correction territory — yet.
You shouldn’t be surprised if one comes.
Historically, the STI has fallen by 10% or more in around eight out of every 10 years.
Was Citi right to call OCBC a sell?
Citi expects OCBC’s third-quarter earnings to come in flat year on year after an exceptional second quarter.
It also expects higher fixed deposit rates to squeeze OCBC’s margins, and it questions OCBC’s valuation.
Here’s the thing: before Wednesday’s downgrade, OCBC shares were already far above their typical valuation multiple.
Before Wednesday’s downgrade, investors were paying around 2.3 times book value.
For context, the shares have historically averaged at roughly 1.2 times.
At 2.3 times, the market just needed a reason to sell.
Any reason would do.
All three banks were due for a pullback on valuation alone, whether Citi said so or someone else did.
On Friday (9 October 2026), OCBC traded at around 2.1 times book value.
To put it simply, the shares are cheaper, but they are far from cheap.
Has anything changed inside the banks?
The short answer is no.
The banks last reported in early August, and those numbers still stand.
In the first half of 2026 (1H 2026), OCBC grew total income by 11% year on year to S$8 billion.
Net interest income fell 3% as the bank’s interest margin narrowed from 1.98% a year ago to 1.73% in 1H 2026.
Non-interest income more than made up the gap.
It rose 36% to S$3.51 billion, backed by net fee income, which grew 26% to S$1.41 billion.
OCBC raised its interim ordinary dividend by 15% to S$0.47 per share, representing a payout of 50% of profit.
Management still expects total income to grow in 2026.
It expects net interest income to dip slightly.
On the flip side, the US Federal Reserve raised
interest rates
in September 2026 for the first time since July 2023, a move that could slow the decline in margins over time.
We’ll have to wait for management to comment on its outlook when OCBC reports its next earnings.
What should you watch when the banks report?
The banks should report third-quarter results in late October or early November.
On the lending side, expect net interest margins to keep slipping.
At the same time, you want loan growth to be strong enough to offset that decline.
OCBC currently expects to deliver high-single to low-double-digit loan growth in 2026.
On the non-lending side, watch whether wealth management fees and insurance income keep growing.
Get Smart: Think in years, not quarters
Think beyond the next set of results.
You want any rise in the share price to come from business growth, not just optimism.
Over the
long term
, the business, not the multiple, should drive your returns.
If the business delivers and the share price still falls, you get to buy more of it at a lower multiple.

title: LVMH sales at key unit fall as China woes hurt Louis Vuitton
article:
(Oct 12): LVMH’s biggest division posted a slump in sales last quarter as its key Louis Vuitton brand suffered from a boycott in China.

Organic revenue at the fashion and leather goods unit slid 5% in the third quarter, LVMH Moët Hennessy Louis Vuitton SE said in a statement on Monday. Analysts were expecting a drop of 1.57%.

The division was “affected in the third quarter by the slowdown in demand in China,” LVMH said.

Louis Vuitton sales suffered in July and August in China after the brand won a trademark dispute against Molly Tea, a local tea maker, Bloomberg reported last month. The victory drew a backlash from Chinese consumers there who deemed it unfair of the world’s largest luxury group to take the much smaller company to court.

LVMH shares have fallen by more than 40% this year, putting them on track for the worst annual performance since the global financial crisis in 2008. While much of the industry is feeling the effects of the downturn in demand, LVMH’s stock is the worst performer this year among major luxury groups, followed by rival Hermes International SCA.

Hopes for a rebound in the wider luxury industry this year have been undermined by sluggish Chinese demand, the prolonged conflict in the Middle East and weaker consumer confidence.

title: US mortgage bond funds suffer one of worst  outflows since 2021
article:
(Oct 12): Investors fled US mortgage bond funds at historic levels over the past three weeks, with outflows ranking among the seven worst since the start of 2021, as surging interest rates spur a flight from volatility.

The Bloomberg US Mortgage Backed Securities Index marked its second worst performance on record in September. The selling follows a spike in Treasury yields to multi-decade highs, fuelled by surging oil prices, inflation concerns, and expectations of Federal Reserve interest rate hikes.

Mortgage-backed securities are highly sensitive to sudden fluctuations in bond yields, which serve as the benchmarks for borrowing costs throughout the economy. When interest rates rise, homeowners tend to stop refinancing their home loans, keeping investors locked into lower-yielding securities for longer than they may had previously expected.

“Fed policy tightening and a flatter curve may reduce demand from banks, a key source of MBS demand,” Erica Adelberg, senior MBS strategist at Bloomberg Intelligence, wrote. “On the positive side, MBS supply should trend lower into year-end, with the highest mortgage rates since 2023 reducing refinancing and home-purchase demand and potentially slowing home-price and loan-size appreciation.”

The Treasuries selloff in September sent yields on long-dated bonds to 24-year highs. Coupled with the underperformance in mortgage-backed securities on an excess return basis, the MBS index logged the second-most negative year-to-date total return in its 50-year history, Adelberg said.

title: Starbucks says it’s not buying Chipotle, dousing deal rumours
article:
(Oct 12): Starbucks Corp said it’s not buying Chipotle Mexican Grill Inc, seeking to tamp down speculation about what could have been one of the restaurant sector’s largest-ever deals.

The company issued a statement on Monday following a report last week that Starbucks, run by former Chipotle chief executive officer Brian Niccol, had worked on a takeover proposal.

At the time, the coffee chain said it was “laser focused” on executing its ongoing turnaround plan, which has revived sales growth after a lengthy slump.

Chipotle shares fell 3.1% as of 9.42am in New York trading on Monday while Starbucks shares were little changed. The burrito chain’s stock had jumped following last week’s report.

Analysts had expressed scepticism about a potential deal, given how different the two businesses are.

At Chipotle, Niccol also spearheaded a revitalisation that turned the company into one of the restaurant industry’s top performers for several years.

See also: Lindt to cut prices as chocolate demand wanes in key markets

The company has recently struggled with sales declines, which it has started to reverse with more frequent product launches and updates to its loyalty programme.

title: SoftBank-backed OPay eyes up to US$500 mil in New York listing — Bloomberg
article:
(Oct 12): SoftBank Group Corp-backed OPay Digital Services Ltd plans to raise about US$500 million with its private placement and an initial public offering in New York, according to people familiar with the matter.

 

The total includes US$200 million from a parallel private placement with Standard Bank Group Ltd, said the people, who asked to remain anonymous as the information is still private.

OPay declined to comment on the matter.

OPay is emerging as one of Africa’s most valuable fintech companies and a dominant player in Nigeria’s fast-growing digital payments sector, with more than 50 million active users monthly.

The listing of the company — which is also backed by HSG, the China division of Sequoia Capital that separated from the investing giant in 2023 — will also involve the sale of new shares to raise funds, said the people.

The transaction will provide a valuation benchmark for the continent’s venture-backed technology sector, which has struggled with fundraising and muted deal activity since the post-pandemic slowdown in private capital markets.

Africa, which is home to the world’s youngest and most rapidly expanding population, has proven a breeding ground for fintechs looking to bridge a gap left by insufficient banking infrastructure.

See also: Is Grab singing the wrong tune for Atome?

OPay will provide US investors with an opportunity to gain exposure to one of the continent’s largest payments platforms and the digitisation of financial services across Africa.

Citigroup Inc, Deutsche Bank AG, Standard Bank and China International Capital Corp will be working on the listing, according to a Friday filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission. It’s expected before the end of the year, according to the people familiar with the transaction.

title: Microsoft bets on homegrown Maia AI chip to challenge Nvidia
article:
SAN FRANCISCO, the US (Oct 12): Microsoft said on Monday it will roll out its in-house Maia artificial intelligence (AI) chips on a massive scale starting in 2027, making them the main hardware for running AI across its products — a move that could reduce its reliance on Nvidia.

Chips like Maia are the technology inside the vast data centres powering the AI boom, and Microsoft plans to deploy enough of them to draw several gigawatts of electricity — roughly the output of several large nuclear reactors.

Nvidia has held a near-lock on the chips used to train AI models, but tech giants and rival chipmakers are now racing to stake out positions in inference — the work of running those models to answer questions and carry out tasks once they are up-and-running.

That market is expanding fast as companies roll out AI assistants and so-called agents that perform multi-step jobs on their own, with Nvidia, AMD, Amazon and Google all pushing out new products in the space.

"Today marks a new phase for Microsoft’s AI infrastructure," Microsoft executive vice president Scott Guthrie wrote in a blog post announcing the plans.

The company said the Maia 200 chip is already operational, including for the Microsoft 365 Copilot assistant, while a more powerful successor, the Maia 300, will launch in 2027.

See also: TikTok’s Chew and Microsoft’s Althoff warn about runaway AI hype

Maia 200 runs models from OpenAI, Microsoft’s own in-house MAI models and leading open-source models.

The chip is deployed in the US, Europe and Australia, and delivers up to 1.7 times more output per watt than leading GPU-based systems for AI features built into Teams and Copilot, according to the company.

Microsoft said the Maia 300 will squeeze 40% more AI work out of the same amount of electricity than leading systems, and more than twice as much as its own previous chip.

See also: DBS CEO Tan says market repricing risks on AI financing

Energy efficiency has become a central concern for tech companies racing to build data centres, as the electricity demands of AI strain power grids and drive up costs.

Each server rack, a cabinet-sized unit in a data centre, will hold 96 of the chips, twice as many as before, and handle up to seven times the workload, the company said.

The new chip’s computing components will be manufactured by Taiwan’s TSMC.

In a separate post, Microsoft engineers said a big focus was cutting the power wasted moving data back and forth inside the machines, a growing problem as AI tools handle more complex tasks.

The systems are mostly cooled with liquid, but Microsoft said they can also run in older data centres cooled by air.

title: TikTok’s Chew and Microsoft’s Althoff warn about runaway AI hype
article:
SINGAPORE (Oct 12): The world may be overexcited by the potential of artificial intelligence (AI) and overlooking its immaturity, tech leaders warned on Monday, arguing that cybersecurity is a bigger near-term issue than AI developing too quickly.

TikTok chief executive officer Shou Chew stressed the advantage that humans continue to have over AI in many areas of creative work at an event in Singapore. The nuances of visual recognition and long-term memory retrieval are still better done by people, he said. At a separate event in the city, Microsoft Corp executive Judson Althoff expressed a similar sentiment urging a sober approach.

Both added to a shift in tone from leading tech companies, which have recently sought to tamp down expectations for the imminent benefits and threats of AI. That’s after they’ve invested hundreds of billions of dollars into AI development and infrastructure.

“On the one hand, I think the technology is not there yet,” Chew said at a conference organised by DBS Bank. “Our brain can do things that the model still cannot.”

Companies are now seeking to strike a balance between evangelising adoption and selling AI products without scaring off customers and the public with the potential pitfalls of such transformative technology.

“I want to separate the hype from the reality of it,” Althoff, the head of Microsoft’s commercial business, said at the company’s event across town. “There’s no path where somehow this notion of infinite cognitive compute capability replaces human purpose.”

See also: DBS CEO Tan says market repricing risks on AI financing

Althoff urged the industry to aim for the same level of trust that people extend to a plumber or a handyman visiting their home. Echoing remarks from the leaders of Anthropic PBC and OpenAI in recent weeks — who both attended a meeting on AI safety with other top executives organised by US President Donald Trump — he added that “observability at every layer of the organisation, and every layer of the stack, is super critical.”

TikTok’s Chew, who oversees one of the world’s most influential social networks, put the emphasis on better understanding the cybersecurity risks of AI, which he said are “quite real” in the short run as companies race to adopt the technology.

title: HSBC moves to Wall Street bonus model, cuts fixed-pay deals
article:
(Oct 12): HSBC Holdings Plc will phase out fixed-pay allowances for its senior staff and instead hand out a greater proportion of its compensation in the form of bonuses, becoming the latest UK lender to switch to Wall Street-style remuneration to better align with performance.

The London-headquartered bank will switch to the new pay system at the start of 2028, according to a memo seen by Bloomberg News.

The approach “strengthens our ability to pay for performance, better differentiate, attract the best talent, and recognise” top performers, a spokesman for HSBC said in a statement.

HSBC’s shift follows a similar update from Barclays Plc, which said in July it would switch more of its employees’ pay towards bonuses after the UK changed its rules around compensation last year, in an effort to boost domestic competitiveness. Wall Street bankers have typically received the bulk of their pay through bonuses tied to performance, rather than fixed salaries.

The planned compensation overhaul is part of a broader restructuring HSBC has seen since Georges Elhedery took over as chief executive officer in September 2024. His shake-up of the lender has resulted in the sale, closing or merger of several businesses and hundreds of job cuts.

The CEO has also led a cost-cutting programme that has included paring back long-time benefits enjoyed by some of the company’s staff such as education allowances and contributions to private club memberships for employees of its Hong Kong-based business.

See also: Healey needs £35 bil to meet UK spending plans, institute says

In Hong Kong, the lender ended a long-standing education subsidy covering 95% of school fees for the children of new hires and senior staff relocating to the city. Existing band-three employees and managing directors who already receive the benefit will retain it. Bloomberg News reported last month. It is also cutting a perk worth up to HK$200,000 that subsidised some private club access for its bankers in the Asian hub.

The share price of HSBC has more than doubled since Elhedery became CEO.

title: Tycoon says Taiwan’s tech boom is filling up his luxury hotels
article:
(Oct 12): A surge in travel fuelled by Taiwan’s artificial intelligence (AI) boom is driving record results at Formosa International Hotels Corp, highlighting the technology sector’s growing impact beyond the island’s chip industry.

The company, led by hospitality tycoon Steven Pan, is on track for record revenue and profit this year, he said in an interview at the Forbes Global CEO Conference in Singapore on Thursday. Room revenue has increased 10% year-to-date, while sales at its luxury retail business have jumped 20% due to the AI boom, he said, declining to provide specific figures.

“What it means for the hotel industry is a tremendous increase in business travel because people have to come and buy stuff from Taiwan, make deals in Taiwan,” Pan said.

Beyond corporate travel, demand for luxury retail business is being driven largely by newly affluent domestic customers, whose spending power has been boosted by strong economic growth and a surging stock market, he added.

Taiwan raised its economic growth forecast for the year to more than 10%, putting the island on track for its first double-digit expansion since 2010 as demand tied to AI continues to fuel the chip hub’s economy. The upgraded outlook follows growth of 8.76% last year.

The AI-driven boom has also made Taiwan a standout destination for equity investors. Taiwan’s benchmark stock index has surged more than 70% this year, making it the top performer among more than 90 equity gauges tracked by Bloomberg.

See also: Pan Pacific Hotels adding 10 new-build hotels and renovation projects across Southeast Asia in 2027

International luxury hotel operators are expanding their presence in Taiwan, including InterContinental, which opened a new hotel in Taipei this month.

Pan plans to open two hotels next year in Linkou, a district in New Taipei City he describes as a future technology hub, as companies including ASML Holding NV and Micron Technology Inc expand their presence in the area. He is also looking to buy a luxury hotel in San Francisco, another tech hub.

“We are looking at undervalued luxury hotels in major gateway cities in America,” Pan said, declining to comment on the deal size. The group also plans to open two hotels in Japan next year.

title: Goldman strategists upgrade global stocks on earnings boost
article:
(Oct 12): Goldman Sachs Group Inc strategists are turning positive on global stocks for the short term, citing a boost from strong earnings for markets already trading near all-time highs.

Equity prices are less demanding after higher oil prices and bond yields stalled the rally, while the outlook for profits is still healthy, the team led by Christian Mueller-Glissmann wrote in a note. They raised their three-month view on stocks to overweight from neutral, matching their bullish stance over a 12-month timeline.

“Earnings growth remains supportive for equities and the recent valuation de-rating has improved asymmetry into the third-quarter earnings season,” Mueller-Glissmann said.

The equity market is set for a high-stakes reporting season that will be crucial to sustaining the rally through to year-end. Analysts expect S&P 500 companies to post a 25% jump in third-quarter profits compared with a year earlier, among the best rates of increase on record, according to data compiled by Bloomberg Intelligence.

The Goldman strategists expect stocks to surpass even that high bar.

See also: US stocks edge higher as oil slips, AI bubble fears recede

The Goldman team prefers a “barbell strategy” of global tech names with selective rate-sensitive, bond-proxy stocks that have derated since the summer. They remain overweight on Asia and the US, and underweight on Europe.

They still view higher rates and energy prices as the main near-term risk to stocks, while the US midterm elections could also boost volatility.

The strategists remain neutral on bonds over three months, but have switched to overweight over 12 months. Allocations to bonds are becoming more attractive to those with longer investment horizons, they said.

See also: US stocks fall from all-time highs on inflation worry

“We believe bonds should gradually move from portfolio headwind to hedge,” they noted.

title: India inflation hits two-year high, backs RBI tightening
article:
(Oct 12): India’s inflation accelerated to an almost two-year high in September, nearing the top of the central bank’s 2% to 6% tolerance band and reinforcing its decision to lift interest rates last week for the first time in almost four years.

The consumer price index rose 5.54% last month from a year earlier, the highest since late 2024, and up from a revised 4.83% in August, data released Monday by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation showed. That was broadly in-line with the 5.58% median estimate in a Bloomberg survey of economists.

Indian government bonds held onto losses after the release, with the benchmark 10-year yield trading around 10 basis points higher at 7.40%. The rupee is up 1% on Monday, though it remains one of the worst-performing currencies in Asia to date.

The combination of rising inflation and a weaker currency is particularly challenging for the country’s central bank as a falling rupee makes imports more expensive, just as price pressures are broadening. The RBI expects inflation to average 6% in the three months through December and raised its full-year forecast to 5.2%.

Monday’s reading comes just days after the Reserve Bank of India’s monetary policy committee voted unanimously to raise its benchmark rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% and shifted its stance to “calibrated tightening.”

See also: Blackouts hit Indian factories as coal crunch feeds into economy

“Amid continued stickiness in commodity prices and rising global yields, we expect RBI to continue to remain firmly on the path of rate hikes,” said Garima Kapoor, economist at Elara Securities. She sees two more rate increases by end-March.

September’s acceleration was driven largely by food inflation, which climbed to 7.74% from 5.97% in August. The category makes up more than a third of the retail inflation basket, and deficient rainfall is expected to add to price pressures in coming months.

Elevated global oil prices remain a worry. The government has largely shielded consumers from the increase at the pump, raising retail fuel prices only modestly in May even as crude has climbed back above US$100 a barrel.

See also: Ambani’s Jio said to seek about US$114 bil valuation in IPO

Businesses have still felt the squeeze. Higher food and energy costs have raised their expenses and eroded margins, with producers so far absorbing much of the increase rather than passing it on to consumers.

“A broad-based food shock is more persistent and carries a greater risk of feeding into household inflation expectations than a temporary increase in vegetable prices,” said Kunal Kundu, an economist with Societe Generale, in a note.
• Transport costs climbed 5.01% from a year earlier, compared with 4.6% in August.

title: Blackouts hit Indian factories as coal crunch feeds into economy
article:
(Oct 12): Indian factories, smelters and households are being hit by blackouts and rising energy costs as the impact of plunging coal stockpiles at the country’s power stations ripples through the economy.

The weakest monsoon since 2015 has curbed hydropower output while hotter-than-normal weather has buoyed demand for air conditioning and farm irrigation. That’s seen coal-fired power stations, which supply about two-thirds of India’s electricity, rapidly burn through their inventories.

Smaller factories, farmers and households are facing power cuts as demand outweighs supply on the grid. Meanwhile, large industrial customers — in metals smelting, chemicals and paper — cannot get enough fuel to produce electricity themselves due to state-owned miner Coal India Ltd prioritising deliveries to grid-connected generators.

Small steel mills in the central state of Chhattisgarh are facing outages of 10 to 12 hours a day, forcing plants to reduce output, said Manish Dhuppad, general secretary at the Chhattisgarh Mini Steel Plant Association.

Mills require an “uninterrupted supply of power", he said. “Say we have hot metal inside the furnace and just before we are able to take it out, the power supply goes. By the time it comes back, the material has solidified and we need to melt it again.”

See also: Ambani’s Jio said to seek about US$114 bil valuation in IPO

The power shortage highlights the increasing role that extreme weather is having on India’s economy, with the weak monsoon driven by a record El Niño. It also shows how the country’s continued reliance on fossil fuels is limiting its ability to respond to a changing climate.

Feedstock supplies at almost half of India’s coal-fired plants had fallen to less than a quarter of required levels as of Oct 10, according to the power ministry. A late burst of monsoon rainfall last month in coal-mining regions in the east of the country exacerbated the shortages, crimping production and also hampering rail transport of the fuel.

In the northern state of Punjab, homes and industries are enduring lengthy blackouts.

See also: World Bank lifts India GDP view, says Asia’s buffers too thin

Badish Jindal, who runs a steel wire plant in Ludhiana, an industrial city in the state, said frequent power cuts of three to four hours had resulted in higher energy costs, as his factory needed to shift to expensive backup generators.

“The power cuts are unscheduled,” he said. “That makes it difficult to plan our operations and deliveries and affects product quality. The sudden stoppage and restart of machines as the power supply goes and comes back also raises the risks of accidents.”

The country’s electricity grid has faced an average shortfall of nearly 4GW a day in the first 10 days of October, data from the Grid Controller of India show. That’s enough to power about two million rural Indian households, according to Bloomberg calculations.

The policy to favour grid-connected power stations has left companies that generate their own coal-fired electricity at a major disadvantage, said Rajiv Agarwal, secretary general of the Indian Captive Power Producers Association, which represents the big industrial users.

They are having to pay high prices at Coal India auctions and buy expensive power from the grid, he said. The firms are also having to wait months for rail transport, so those with limited operating capital are being forced to cut output, he said.

Average premiums at Coal India spot sales in September jumped to 94% over the base price, compared with a 59% difference in August. Two of the company’s subsidiaries — Northern Coalfields and South Eastern Coalfields — charged more than a 200% premium at auctions last month, data from the miner show.
